name: Low-Profile Keyboard
description: A low-profile 75-percent mechanical keyboard machined from a single billet of slate-grey anodised aluminium: a flat slab about 320 millimetres wide by 130 deep, standing 18 millimetres at the rear and tapering to a 12 millimetre front lip, its top plane meeting the flanks along a bright polished micro-bevel that runs unbroken around the case, its four corners carrying one generous identical radius, its key block set in a narrow aluminium border of exactly equal width on all four sides, with low-profile matte PBT keycaps in a two-tone scheme of off-white alphas against slate-grey modifiers, one knurled slate aluminium rotary knob at the top-right corner, and neutral white backlighting beneath the caps.
materials: unibody slate-grey anodised aluminium case, bead-blasted matte on every face with a bright polished chamfer where the top plane meets the flanks, low-profile matte PBT keycaps in off-white and slate grey with a shallow cylindrical dish and crisp moulded edges, low-profile mechanical switches, a knurled slate aluminium rotary knob with a chamfered rim and evenly milled ridges, four dark-grey rubber feet inset flush into the base
primaryColors: slate grey anodised aluminium, off-white PBT keycaps, slate-grey PBT modifiers, neutral white backlight
negativeConstraints: never render any text, logo, wordmark, engraving, or printing anywhere on the aluminium case, the flanks, the rotary knob, or the underside; keep every keycap completely blank unless the art direction explicitly calls for lit backlit legends, and where it does, render exactly one plain uppercase sans-serif character on each alpha keycap and nothing more, never a word, never a multi-character string, never a phrase, never an icon, arrow, symbol, or brand mark, and never a legend on any modifier, function, or navigation cap; never render a numeric keypad, a second rotary knob, a full-size layout, an RGB rainbow spill, tall sculpted high-profile keycaps, a visible seam splitting the case, uneven gaps between caps, sharp unradiused corners, or an aluminium border wider on one side of the key block than another; never swap the anodised slate aluminium for plastic or the PBT caps for glossy translucent ones, and never lose the two-tone off-white and slate scheme; never reproduce the silhouette, badge, key shape, hinge, or trade dress of any real keyboard or computer manufacturer's product Exception: a mark, wordmark, or label that the brief's art direction explicitly names is deliberate and must be rendered exactly as directed — the text bans above apply only to invented marks the art direction never asked for.
preservationNotes: the unibody slate-grey anodised aluminium case with its bead-blasted matte faces, its bright polished micro-bevel running unbroken where the top plane meets the flanks, its low 12 millimetre front lip rising to 18 millimetres at the rear, its one generous corner radius repeated on all four corners and its roughly 320 by 130 millimetre footprint, the 75-percent layout with one row of function keys along the top, a dedicated arrow cluster at the lower right, a single column of four navigation keys along the right edge and no numeric pad, the two-tone scheme of off-white alpha caps against slate-grey modifier caps, the identical gap between every keycap and the identical narrow aluminium border on all four sides of the key block, the one knurled slate aluminium rotary knob at the top-right corner with its chamfered rim, the single USB-C port centred on the rear edge in a chamfered machined cutout, the four flush rubber feet in the base, and the neutral white backlighting must read identically in every angle, same case height, key spacing and knob position throughout When the art direction explicitly names a mark on this product, that named mark is part of the product's identity for that shot and overrides the blank-surface requirement.
